needs_attention: BACKTEST RUN -- generated 2026-09-10 against the 2026-09-02 ingest as evidence for un-parking criteria 1 and 2. Not for execution. No approvals.json was created, read, or pre-populated.

HEADLINE: the ranking class order plus the 25-action cap made this plan homogeneous. 49 drift findings produced 49 candidate actions; the R3 (stale_approaching) class alone holds 32 and ranks ahead of every other class, so all 25 slots are `call` actions. Every draft_followup, every escalation and both categorization reviews were cut. requires_write_count is 0 -- nothing routes to ghl-actions-agent today.

Overflow: 24 actions dropped by the 25-action cap. Top 5 overflow items by rank: Elsa Espejo (92% of threshold), Rafay A. Wasay (92%), Jayanathan Kuhananthan (92%), Gopal (86%), Raman Aggarwal (83%). The remaining 17 are the entire R1 class (12 meeting_no_followup), the entire R4 class (3 abandonment_next) and the entire R5 class (2 categorization_miss).

Dropped but Albert should still see them: Zinat Hirji is 83.9d PAST her auto-abandon point (263.9d in '1b. Postponed' vs 180d, 147%) -- an R4 escalation that never reached the list, and one the ingest itself raised. noel brillantes and Ali Merali are the other two abandonment_next findings.

Also dropped: both R5 categorization reviews -- Karvin Cheung (3 connected calls, no tag, no opportunity, address SMS failed to deliver) and unknown caller (647) 917-8253. And all 12 R1 meeting_no_followup findings, including Mizanur Bhuiyan at 39.7d overdue. The ingest notes no follow-up sequence exists for the Meeting-Scheduled stage at all.

The cap cuts through a tie. Four findings sit at exactly 92% of threshold (Harj Heer, Ushi Masrani, Elsa Espejo, Rafay A. Wasay); two landed at ranks 24-25 and two overflowed purely on tie-break. Whether that split is acceptable is a judgment call for Albert, not a derivation.

Tie-break gap (flag, not resolved): the specified tie-break 'earlier first_contact wins' is not implementable -- first_contact appears only in extensions.ghl.won_records, never on open opportunities. The second tie-break (project before store) never binds, since the STORE pipeline defines no staleness thresholds and produced no findings. Ties were broken by the ingest's own workflow_drift array order: deterministic and idempotent, but it is a stand-in, not the stated rule.

Rule-table gap -- no per-entity dedup. 5 opportunities generated BOTH an R3 call and an R1 draft_followup for the same entity (Mizanur Bhuiyan, Shahid Khan, Harry, Baljit Grewal, Siham Mohamed). Only the 25-action cap prevented double outreach on those contacts today. On a lighter day the same plan would ask Albert to call and to text the same person for the same underlying staleness.

R2 (untagged_in_queue) and R6 (followup_not_fired) produced zero actions -- no findings of either type exist in workflow_drift. But metrics.untagged_in_queue reads 8, and reporting.exclusions.drift_excluded_by_stage suppresses 10 untagged_in_queue findings at stage '0a. New Lead'. R2 is structurally unreachable against this ingest shape, and the count of 8 vs 10 suppressed does not reconcile.

Contract gap -- finding ids. 39 of the 49 workflow_drift entries are not itemized in `items` (they sit behind the '+60 lower-priority items' rollup) and carry no id field of their own. basis.item_id for those was constructed on ingest's own `ghl-drift-<type>-<ref>` pattern. ingest-schema.md should give every workflow_drift entry an explicit stable id rather than leaving the planner to reconstruct one.

Contract gap -- entity ids. 10 of the 25 actions carry ghl_contact_id: null. workflow_drift[].ref is an OPPORTUNITY id, and no opportunity-to-contact mapping exists for findings that aren't itemized. Names were deliberately NOT matched against extensions.ghl.conversations to fill the gap -- that is the fragile inference the contract exists to prevent. All ids emitted are the 20-char alphanumeric form; no dashed UUID or 24-char hex appeared anywhere.

Contract gap -- id stability. Action ids here are a deterministic composite, `plan-<rule_id>-<opportunity id>`, not a cryptographic hash. The planner's tool grant is Read/Write with no Bash, so it cannot compute a hash; inventing hex that looks like one would break the exact property the rule protects, because a later run could not reproduce it. The composite is stable, unique and re-derivable. plan-schema.md and the agent file should say 'deterministic function of' rather than 'hash of', or the planner needs a hashing tool.

LARGEST GAP FOUND: the rule table covers only the six drift types, so nothing in extensions.ghl.conversations can ever become an action. That silences 11 of the ingest's own top-13 stragglers_ranked items -- Diego Contecha waiting to be told his balance, Mohammad Abd Bint Azi's corrected final total, Naveen Sharma's price ask and Wednesday site visit, Wanda's 3 missed calls this morning, Damian's warranty date, Sean K's balance reply, Priya Chotrani's photo request, Mario's promised stairs quote, install scheduling for Silviya Jardany's won project, Ashrim Narsinh's flooring-noise warranty complaint, and Rachita Saini's planned Thursday order. Every one is a same-day commitment; none is a drift type; none can be planned.

No rule covers data hygiene either: the 'Albert Ngo' contact whose phone matches Titan's own main line (data-quirk flag), and 17 STORE: Material Pipeline records sitting in Closed-Won/Closed-Lost stages with opportunity.status still 'open'.
